title: Maaw maa, Naaw nuu, and Long a

slides.heading: Two letters, one shared shape
body: ม and น both carry the same low, husky "m" and "n" sounds you already make in English — no aspiration, no surprise.
Each glyph is one loop hung off a tall stem. The whole difference between them is which shoulder the loop sits on.
ม keeps its loop on the left shoulder. น swings it over to the right.

slides.heading: Same class, same tone habits
body: ม and น both belong to the low consonant class, so they will follow the same tone rules once those rules arrive in lesson two.
For now the class is just a label to notice: low, low — every low-class letter after them behaves the same way.

slides.prompt: ม and น are mirror images of each other. Which shoulder does ม's loop sit on, and which shoulder does น's?

answers: ม: left shoulder. น: right shoulder.

slides.heading: The long vowel า
body: The vowel sign า trails a consonant and stretches its sound into a long, open "aa" — hold it until it runs out of breath.
It never stands alone; it always rides behind the consonant that starts the syllable.

slides.heading: นา — rice farm
body: Put น in front of the long vowel: น plus า makes นา.
นา (naa) means a rice farm or a field — one of the first nouns a farmer's child ever hears.

slides.prompt: น plus the long vowel — what word does that spell, and what does it mean?

answers: นา — naa — a rice farm or a field.

slides.heading: มา — to come
body: Swap the consonant: ม plus the same long vowel makes มา.
มา (maa) means "to come" — a verb you will reach for constantly from here on.

slides.prompt: Swap นา's first consonant for ม. What word do you get, and what does it mean?

slides.heading: นาน — a long time
body: Close the syllable with a second น: น plus the vowel plus น makes นาน.
นาน (naan) means "a long time" — the same vowel, now bookended by two low-class letters.

slides.prompt: Bookend the long vowel with น on both sides. What word does that spell, and what does it mean?

answers: นาน — naan — a long time.
